scene_record_side_blocks.question: What fills the 0x120 side blocks and the count at record+988h; docs/MISSION_LOAD_PATH.md found no write in the .scn reader's reconstruction.
scene_record_side_blocks.answer: The writer is not in the reader's grammar. 00469bf0's `properties` branch parses a 0x114 property bag with 008f5a00, publishes it as SceneRootProps and runs the applier 004f1d70, which at 004f21b4..004f21e3 calls 004e82f0 eight times with ECX = slot index and EDX = the bag's MultiPlay sub-block. The blocks are the multiplayer player-slot definitions authored in the scene file.

scene_record_side_blocks.case_insensitivity: 008f2260 looks keys up through 0043b8b0, which compares with __stricmp. The applier passes "MultiPlay" and every shipped .scn spells the block "Multiplay"; a case-sensitive compare would leave every side block unwritten.

singleton.abi: no arguments, returns the pool in EAX, no stack cleanup; callers push the arguments of the following thiscall first

release.abi: __thiscall(pool; void* block, uint size, uint unused), RET 0xc
release.note: sized release; the caller must pass the size the block was allocated with, always length + 1 here

scene_record_storage.model_verdict: src/mission_load_path.cpp's std::string model reproduces every value this path reads or compares, including the duplicate test, because 004e1f0x substitutes the zeroed global 00e18b1c for a null data pointer and that compares like "". Not corrected.
model_boundaries: The empty string has a null data pointer, not a pointer to "". Every native reader in this path guards with `if (data != 0)` or substitutes 00e18b1c.
0041dd4a returns immediately when the requested length equals the stored length, even when data is null, so buffer identity and allocation counts are not equivalent to std::string.
There is no capacity, so every length change reallocates; reserve and the growth factor have no counterpart.

scene_class_count_delta.question: The nine-entity difference between the mission-load sweep (133655) and docs/SCENE_ENTITY_FACTORY.md (133664).
scene_class_count_delta.verdict: 133664 is right. The cause is a reader rule difference in the reconstruction, not nested blocks and not a doc error.
scene_class_count_delta.native_rule: 008f5a00 reads a fixed number of value tokens for the type letter it dispatched on and then runs 008d9930 ExpectToken(";"), which peeks and consumes only on a match. A property authored without its terminator costs one reported error and consumes nothing further.
scene_class_count_delta.reconstruction_bug: src/scene_file.cpp parse_property_body scanned values `while (!cur.at(";"))`, so a `;`-less property swallowed the closing brace of the block it was in and every later block nested one level too deep.
scene_class_count_delta.trigger: Runs of four `"PlaneStock n" { Count = ... ; Type = E PlaneClasses : X }` sub-blocks whose Type line has no `;`. The last of each run swallows the sub-block's own `}`; four runs per file put the parser four levels deep at end of input, which is exactly the four `expected }, got "traffic"` errors each file reported.
